title: Playing with Louis Armstrong at Tom Anderson's
summary: In 1910 he worked in the Red Light district at Tom Anderson's saloon in a four-piece band with Armstrong, discussing the location and who else played there.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: The land next? Moraine Custom House. You know where that's? Yes. That was the Red Lake District there in 1910. You know, this would go up. And I worked there. I worked at Tom Anderson's saloon there on Ramport, near Canaro, with Louis Armstrong and I. That's where he started.
Oh, yes, I've heard of that. On Ramport.
Is that place called The Real Thing?
I don't know what it is.
Is that the one that George Delcy ran?

I think it was because they had two. They had one on Custom House Street, you know. They had one on Custom House Street, right on the other side of the basin. And then they had one right near the corner, the canal in Ramport, north Ramport.
Big Ten Cent store there now.
Who else was in the band with Armstrong? That was Armstrong.
That was Armstrong. Ines Trepania playing drum. I know the boy can't call his name, huh? I'm just as good as he can't call his name.
Did you work there with Albert Nicholas ever? Barney Bigard? They worked at that place a while with Paul Barberin.
Barney Bigard and I worked with Sidney Desby. I saw Sidney.
We saw him out in California, too.
I worked with his family a long time, too. I was playing banjo then. I played banjo.
What were the four pieces? What instruments?

That was a violin, guitar, bass, and drum. No, cornet and drum. Violin, guitar, cornet and drum. I was playing violin. Louis Armstrong was playing cornet. And Tom Batten playing guitar. And Ernest Trepania, he used to call them the next.
